raw_response:
I only have 6 mu, so I will keep doing the wheat-maize rotation on all 6 mu, same as the past years. Changing crop is too risky for me. What feeds my family and brings cash is this one round of wheat and one round of maize. I did not go to school, so I do not count things too finely. I look at what happened on my own land and what the neighbors do. If I save too much on fertilizer and the crop turns yellow, then the yield drops and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But money is still tight because some people in the house work outside and cash does not always come at once, so I cannot put too much in at one time.

For wheat, I will sow in early October on the full 6 mu after the maize is off. I will use the local wheat seed people around here commonly plant, not anything fancy, just reliable. I will put most fertilizer as base before sowing, then see the wheat in spring. If the leaves are light and the stand is weak, I will topdress once at jointing. Water from the well costs money, but wheat here cannot rely only on the sky, so I will likely irrigate around sowing, at jointing, and around grain filling if it stays dry. For maize, I will plant right after wheat harvest in June, very fast, because that window is short. I do not want too much tillage between crops because it wastes time and labor. I will use hybrid maize seed because maize seed is usually bought anyway and gives more stable yield. I will put fertilizer once at planting and once when it grows tall enough, and irrigate one or two times depending on rain. If pests show, I spray; if not, I do not waste the money.
